task: Independent comprehensive review of V8 7D bicycle world model

1_data_quality.summary: Data is clean (no NaN/Inf) but has structural issues that may affect model training and evaluation.
positive_findings: 150,000 samples, 8D obs with kappa correctly identified as constant-zero and dropped to 7D
No NaN or Inf values in any array
Action distribution is near-uniform (kurtosis=-1.2, skewness=0.006), good for GP training
Train/test split is 106214/43786 (71%/29%), episodes not split across boundary
concerns: Episode count discrepancy: declared 148 episodes but only 59 actual episodes from done flags. The metadata may refer to sub-episodes before merging. This does not affect training but should be documented.

89 continuity errors found at segment boundaries (max diff ~1.03). These occur at regular ~1500-2000 step intervals, suggesting data collection segment boundaries. Models may learn incorrect transitions at these points.
Speed (v) has extremely low variance (std=0.013, range 0.54-0.66). This makes v trivially easy to predict (all models achieve NMAE < 1e-5) and inflates overall NMAE metrics by contribution averaging.

State e_psi has median=0 with symmetric range [-1,1], suggesting heavy concentration at zero. Same for theta (median=-1), delta (median=-1), delta_dot (median=-1). These concentrated distributions may bias GP models.
Train/test actual ratio is 0.708, not the declared 0.75. The split is sequential (not shuffled by episode), which is correct for time-series but means test set may have different dynamics than train.
1_data_quality.impact_on_results: The low-variance v dimension makes all models appear better than they are on average. The continuity errors at segment boundaries may explain some of the multi-step divergence patterns.

2_interface_correctness.summary: All 10 interface tests pass. All 6 baseline models produce correct (7,) predictions.
2_interface_correctness.note: GP and SINDy do not provide uncertainty estimates, which limits their use for risk-aware planning.

3_single_step_accuracy.source: Agent C (3000 samples) + Agent H (10000 samples)
3_single_step_accuracy.critical_issue: Agent C and Agent H report very different NMAE values for the same GP model. Agent C GP NMAE=0.0321 vs Agent H GP NMAE=0.00166. This 20x discrepancy suggests different evaluation protocols (different random seeds, data subsets, or normalization). Agent H's GP results showing e_y NMAE=0.0 and e_psi NMAE=0.0 are suspicious and may indicate data leakage or evaluation on training data.

rde_m.note: Diverged: DAgger training produced numerically unstable model

gp.suspicious: e_y=0.0, e_psi=0.0 NMAE is implausibly perfect

gp_ensemble_5.note: WORSE than single GP, ensemble adds cost without benefit

gp_ensemble_7.note: Marginally better than ensemble-5 but 2x cost

rde_l.critical: IDENTICAL to E1 - likely a bug where same model is used for both

4_multi_step_rollout.note: Agent E uses 5 segments x 200 steps; Agent H uses 3 segments x 200 steps. Different segment counts may affect variance estimates.

short_horizon_H1_to_H10.observation: Neural ODE is 3-4x better than GP-based methods at short horizons

medium_horizon_H10_to_H50.observation: GP Ensemble shows significant improvement over single GP at medium horizons. Neural ODE maintains best stability.

long_horizon_H50_to_H100.observation: E1/RDE-L diverge severely at H=100 (NMAE=3.03). Single GP diverges (NMAE=1.98). Neural ODE is 5x better than single GP.

divergence_analysis.gp_H100: NMAE=1.98 (DIVERGED, e_psi saturates at 1.0, delta_dot explodes)
divergence_analysis.e1_H100: NMAE=3.03 (WORST divergence, residual NN compounds errors)
divergence_analysis.neural_ode_H100: NMAE=0.407 (STABLE, continuous dynamics prevent discrete error accumulation)

calibration_metrics.interpretation: Uncertainties are ~51x too small. After scaling by 51x, coverage reaches 95%. ECE of 0.163 indicates poor calibration (ideal=0). Pearson r=0.413 shows moderate correlation between uncertainty and error, meaning the uncertainty direction is somewhat informative but magnitude is wrong.

v_noteworthy.note: Near-zero correlation - uncertainty is uninformative for speed

ood_detection_broken.problem: ALL 43786 test samples are classified as OOD (any |s_i| > 2*std_i). This makes AUROC/AUPRC meaningless. The OOD definition is too aggressive for normalized states.
ood_detection_broken.impact: OOD detection capability is unvalidated. Cannot assess model reliability on out-of-distribution inputs.

6_mpc_planning.summary: Model predictions do not reliably rank candidate trajectories, making MPPI-style planning ineffective.

key_metrics.interpretation: Near-zero ranking correlation means the model cannot distinguish good trajectories from bad ones. The top-8% overlap means only 1 in 10 top trajectories are correct.

cost_prediction.interpretation: Cost predictions have 33-50% error. The model systematically underestimates costs. Cost correlation of 0.71 is moderate but insufficient for planning.

6_mpc_planning.root_cause: Multi-step prediction errors compound rapidly. At H=10, NMAE is already 0.09 (Agent E) / 0.089 (Agent H), and by H=20 it reaches 0.19-0.33. The model cannot accurately predict long-term consequences of actions.

gp_ensemble.finding: Ensembles provide significant multi-step improvement but NOT single-step improvement
gp_ensemble.single_step: GP Ensemble 5 NMAE=0.00180 is WORSE than single GP NMAE=0.00166
gp_ensemble.multi_step_H50: GP Ensemble 5 NMAE=0.507 is 2.6x BETTER than single GP NMAE=1.327
gp_ensemble.multi_step_H100: GP Ensemble 5 NMAE=0.632 is 3.1x BETTER than single GP NMAE=1.980
gp_ensemble.cost: 1384s train time (6.3x single GP), 2675s for ensemble-7 (12.3x)
gp_ensemble.verdict: Ensembles are worth it for multi-step applications (H>=20) despite higher train cost

adaptive_residual.finding: Mixed results - best single-step among residual methods but poor multi-step
adaptive_residual.single_step: NMAE=0.00748, better than E1/RDE-L but worse than GP

neural_ode.finding: Clear winner for multi-step stability despite worse single-step accuracy
neural_ode.verdict: Best method for any application requiring multi-step prediction (H>=5)

neural_ode_multistep.finding: Multi-step training hurts single-step but helps medium horizons
neural_ode_multistep.single_step: NMAE=0.0360, worse than standard Neural ODE
neural_ode_multistep.multi_step_H10: NMAE=0.0557, 2.4x worse than standard Neural ODE
neural_ode_multistep.multi_step_H50: NMAE=0.548, 1.8x worse than standard Neural ODE
neural_ode_multistep.verdict: Standard Neural ODE is better at all horizons. Multi-step training objective does not help.

8_gp_sample_size_analysis.analysis: Going from 2000 to 5000 GP samples costs 6x more training time for only 11.4% NMAE improvement (0.00166 to 0.00147). This is a poor return on investment. The GP model with 2000 samples is already near-optimal for single-step prediction. The bottleneck is not training data quantity but model expressiveness.
8_gp_sample_size_analysis.recommendation: Use GP with 2000 samples for single-step applications. The 5000-sample GP is not worth the cost unless single-step accuracy is the sole critical metric.

critical_issues.issue: E1 and RDE-L produce IDENTICAL results in Agent H
critical_issues.evidence: Agent H single-step: E1 NMAE=0.009979, RDE-L NMAE=0.009979. Multi-step: identical at ALL horizons (H=1 through H=100).
critical_issues.likely_cause: Either (a) RDE-L with dagger_rounds_L=0 is literally the same model as E1, or (b) a bug causes the same model object to be used for both names.

critical_issues.issue: Agent H GP reports NMAE=0.0 for e_y and e_psi
critical_issues.evidence: Agent H single-step GP: e_y mae=0.0, rmse=0.0, nmae=0.0; e_psi same.
critical_issues.likely_cause: Data leakage (evaluating on training data), or the evaluation subset happens to contain only states where GP predicts perfectly.

critical_issues.issue: Agent C and Agent H NMAE values differ by ~20x for same GP model
critical_issues.evidence: Agent C GP NMAE=0.0321 (3000 samples) vs Agent H GP NMAE=0.00166 (10000 samples).
critical_issues.likely_cause: Different evaluation protocols: different random seeds, different data normalization, or Agent H evaluates on an easier subset.

critical_issues.evidence: Agent C: all metrics are NaN, note says 'DAgger training produced numerically unstable model'.
critical_issues.likely_cause: DAgger with dagger_rounds_M=2 causes training instability, likely due to distribution shift amplification.
critical_issues.severity: MEDIUM - one of six baseline models is non-functional

critical_issues.evidence: Agent D: ood_fraction=1.0 (all 43786 test samples classified as OOD).
critical_issues.likely_cause: OOD definition 'any |s_i| > 2*std_i' is too aggressive for normalized states with std~0.5.
critical_issues.severity: MEDIUM - model reliability assessment is impossible

single_step.note: Best single-step per Agent H, but e_y/e_psi=0.0 is suspicious
Worst single-step but fastest after SINDy

issues_found.description: E1 and RDE-L produce identical results across all metrics and horizons. This means either (a) RDE-L with dagger_rounds_L=0 degenerates to E1, or (b) there is a code bug reusing the same model. This invalidates the E1 vs RDE-L comparison.
issues_found.action_required: Verify that RDE-L and E1 are actually different models. If dagger_rounds_L=0 means no DAgger rounds, then RDE-L is just E1 by design and should be documented as such.

issues_found.description: Agent H GP reports NMAE=0.0 for e_y and e_psi states, which is physically implausible for any model. This likely indicates data leakage (evaluating on training data) or a bug in the evaluation pipeline.
issues_found.action_required: Re-run GP single-step evaluation with explicit train/test separation and verify e_y/e_psi errors are non-zero.

issues_found.description: Agent C and Agent H report vastly different NMAE for the same GP model (0.0321 vs 0.00166). The 20x discrepancy suggests fundamentally different evaluation protocols.
issues_found.action_required: Standardize evaluation: same random seed, same data split, same normalization. Report which protocol is authoritative.

issues_found.description: RDE-M (hybrid DAgger) produces all NaN predictions. One of six baseline models is completely non-functional.
issues_found.action_required: Either fix DAgger training stability or exclude RDE-M from comparisons.

issues_found.description: OOD detection classifies 100% of test samples as out-of-distribution, making AUROC undefined. The OOD criterion (|s_i| > 2*std_i) is inappropriate for normalized states.
issues_found.action_required: Use a more meaningful OOD definition (e.g., states from unseen episodes, or states in low-density regions of the training distribution).

issues_found.description: Uncertainty calibration requires 51x scalar scaling to achieve 95% coverage. ECE=0.163 is poor. The raw uncertainty estimates are not usable without post-hoc calibration.
issues_found.action_required: Apply learned calibration scaling before using uncertainties in any downstream application.

issues_found.description: MPC planning shows near-zero ranking correlation (Spearman rho=0.006). The model cannot reliably rank candidate trajectories, making it unsuitable for trajectory optimization.
issues_found.action_required: This is likely a fundamental limitation of single-step models applied to multi-step planning. Consider using the Neural ODE (best multi-step stability) for planning, or accept that planning requires closed-loop replanning at each step.

issues_found.description: Neural ODE MultiStep training does not improve over standard Neural ODE at any horizon. The multi-step training objective appears to hurt performance.
issues_found.action_required: Investigate why multi-step training degrades performance. May need curriculum learning or gradient clipping.

issues_found.description: 89 continuity errors at data segment boundaries. While small (max diff ~1.03), they may cause models to learn incorrect transition dynamics.
issues_found.action_required: Either filter out transition steps or document them as known artifacts.

issues_found.description: Episode count discrepancy: 148 declared vs 59 actual. Does not affect model training but should be documented.

recommendations.action: Fix the E1/RDE-L identity bug or document that RDE-L with 0 DAgger rounds is equivalent to E1
Re-validate GP single-step results to confirm e_y/e_psi errors are non-zero
Standardize evaluation protocol between Agent C and Agent H (same seed, same split, same normalization)
Fix or exclude RDE-M from comparisons
Fix OOD detection to use a meaningful criterion
Apply uncertainty calibration before using in any safety-critical application
For practical deployment: use Neural ODE for multi-step prediction, GP (2000 samples) for single-step prediction
Investigate why Neural ODE MultiStep training degrades performance vs standard Neural ODE

overall_summary.best_single_step: GP (2000 samples) - NMAE=0.0017, but results may be inflated by suspicious e_y/e_psi=0.0 values
overall_summary.best_multi_step: Neural ODE - NMAE=0.407 at H=100, 5x better than GP, 7.5x better than E1
overall_summary.best_practical: Neural ODE for H>=5 (fast training at 144s, best multi-step stability); GP for H=1 (fastest inference)
overall_summary.key_limitation: No method achieves reliable multi-step prediction beyond H=20. All models diverge by H=100 with NMAE > 0.4. Planning (Agent F) is not currently viable.
overall_summary.v8_vs_v6: V8 7D model is 83-413x worse than V6 4D model at H=50 (per Agent E comparison), confirming that the additional dimensions (theta, theta_dot, delta, delta_dot) make the problem significantly harder.
overall_summary.confidence_in_findings: MEDIUM - Multiple cross-agent inconsistencies (E1=RDE-L, GP zero errors, NMAE scale differences) reduce confidence in quantitative rankings. Qualitative findings (Neural ODE best multi-step, ensembles help) are more reliable.
